title: The README shows each feature as a GIF
body:
The README's feature sections hold bold placeholders where a GIF goes: the session picker, the context window, markdown, and marking passages. "a chat that reads like a text thread" shows the still `assets/chat.png`. GIFs go under `assets/`, which `Cargo.toml` already excludes from the crate.

`scenarios/readme/` holds one scenario per feature for `coax-fake-agent` to play, each checked in tmux:

| scenario | what it plays |
|---|---|
| `picker.json` | four earlier sessions, ages 19 hours to a month, each with a short history |
| `thread.json` | a thought, a read, a reply, an edit, a command with output, a second reply, context at 32% |
| `context.json` | one act per prompt, stepping context through 20%, 60%, 85% and 97% |
| `markdown.json` | a heading, a list, a quote, a table, a Rust block too wide for the box, a fenced `markdown` block |
| `marking.json` | a reply with three points, then an answer to `[1]` and `[2]` |

## Proposal

Record each GIF in a decade scratch pane with the `record` tool that decade-7fb578 proposes, then put it in place of its placeholder.

## Open

- The picker's agents row shows the agent's command and arguments. A config that names `coax-fake-agent` by an absolute path puts that path in the recording. The recording config should name the binary bare, with `target/debug` on `PATH`, and the scenario by a relative path.
- The agent's name in that config shows in the picker and in each session row. `fake` reads oddly in a README.
- Until decade-7fb578 lands, `gpu-screen-recorder` and `ffmpeg` can record the pane's region of the screen, measured by hand.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Recording setup, agreed with Jack and checked by screenshot:

- ghostty at `--font-size=18` with `--window-decoration=none`, in a scratch pane dragged to 80 columns by 24 rows. That is 1695 × 1189 pixels inside ghostty, and decade's `record` captures 1749 × 1242.
- `record` with no `width`, so the GIF keeps the captured pixels. 1749 is about twice the width of GitHub's README column, which shows it halved with no blur.
- The scenarios have to fit 24 rows. At 100 columns, the earlier takes left the prompt far to the right of the replies.
- `record` cannot start together with the program, so ghostty sleeps 6 seconds before starting coax. The blank lead-in is cut afterwards.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: `assets/thread.gif` replaces `assets/chat.png` under "a chat that reads like a text thread". It plays `scenarios/readme/thread.json` through `--input` (coax-573e0f), with the folded run of tool calls from coax-d1bcb7 and the status line filled in. 1749 × 1403, 18 seconds, 504 KB. The other four GIFs are still to record.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: All four GIFs are recorded and in the README: `assets/picker.gif`, `assets/thread.gif`, `assets/markdown.gif` and `assets/marking.gif`, 140 to 504 KB each, at 1749 pixels wide. At Jack's word the context-window section and `scenarios/readme/context.json` are dropped, since every GIF shows the context bar. Each GIF plays its scenario through `--input`, mouse steps included (coax-d79a59), in ghostty at font size 18 with `--app-notifications=no-clipboard-copy`, which keeps the copy button from raising a toast in the frame. The picker take runs with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` pointing at a scratch config whose `[agents.claude]` names `coax-fake-agent` bare. Uncommitted.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: Jack changed the plan. The README drops the four GIFs for one longer example GIF that walks through a first session: the picker loads a session, a turn's tool calls fold and a click opens them, a markdown reply gets panned, copied and switched to raw, and two passages are marked and answered. Jack judged coax's drawn pointer (coax-d79a59) too crude, so the mouse in that recording will come from decade's real pointer through decade-82f459. The four GIFs in `assets/` stand until the combined one replaces them.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: `scenarios/readme/tour.json` holds the combined walkthrough. It reuses the sessions from `picker.json`, the tool-call turn from `thread.json`, the reply from `markdown.json` and both acts of `marking.json`, with the context climbing from 15% to 32%. Its `input` loads the second session from the picker, then opens and closes the nine-call group, pans, copies and toggles the code blocks, and marks two passages. For now it uses coax's own mouse steps. It plays through in tmux at 80 × 28 in about 44 seconds, with every click finding its target. The scratch config for the picker now points at `tour.json`. Recording waits for decade-82f459.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: `assets/tour.gif` is in the README at the top of `## features`, and the four separate GIFs are deleted. It plays `scenarios/readme/tour.json`, which `input` retimed from 44 to 18 seconds, still with coax's own pointer. 1749 × 1426, 21.7 seconds, 778 KB. The first take came out at 35 columns because of decade-893ae9, and the retake is at 80 × 28. The other scenario files in `scenarios/readme/` stay until Jack decides whether to keep them.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: `assets/tour.gif` is retaken at 80 × 38: 1749 × 1886, 36 seconds with the end hold, 883 KB. The markdown reply now shows two heading levels, bold, italic, inline code, a link, a numbered list, a nested bullet list, a quote, a rule and a table, besides the two code blocks. The marking turn marks the first and third bullets and types a line after each chip, with `Alt+Enter` between them. Two playback changes made that possible: a key step can carry modifiers, and a negative `nth` counts matches from the bottom, so a `mark` click no longer lands on the word `markdown` higher up. coax now copies the frame for target lookup before drawing its pointer, which had hidden the text under the pointer from the next click.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: The markdown reply's table now has longer filler cells: one wraps onto a second line, one holds inline code and bold, and the numbers vary in width. `assets/tour.gif` is retaken with it, 927 KB.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: The tour now drags the Rust block's scroll-bar thumb to pan the long string into view: `drag` from the start of `━━━` to the block's copy button. Panning moves the block's `rust` label and copy button out of view along with the code. A second drag, back to `wrap`, pans home in tmux, but in the ghostty take the block stayed panned. Nobody has found out why yet. `assets/tour.gif` is that take: 40 seconds, 1.0 MB.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: The fenced `markdown` block in the tour now holds a heading, bold, italic, inline code, a link, a quote and a pipe table, so its raw view differs from the rendered one on almost every line. `assets/tour.gif` is retaken with it, 40 seconds, 1.0 MB.
